purpose: 2D soil-structure interaction analysis of a cut-and-cover underground structure with diaphragm walls and base slab on Winkler spring supports.
Description of Building Structural Syste: Underground H-frame cut-and-cover structure with reinforced concrete diaphragm walls and base slab, supported on compression-only Winkler springs representing surrounding soil.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model using dispBeamColumn elements for diaphragm walls (30 elements each) and base slab (9 elements), with ENT (Elastic No Tension) uniaxial materials for horizontal and vertical Winkler springs across 5 soil layers. Two load cases: uniform earth pressure (15 kPa) and hydrostatic water pressure (triangular distribution). Static analysis with gravity freeze then lateral load application using opst.anlys.SmartAnalyze.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: NA
Notes: ST31 (L2) underground structure model with two selectable lateral load cases: case 1 = uniform earth pressure (15 kPa), case 2 = hydrostatic water pressure (triangular). Model uses --case argument to switch.

purpose: Quasi-static cyclic pushover of a 3D non-ductile RC frame representative of Italian pre-1970s construction (gravity-only design).
Description of Building Structural Syste: Model of a 2/3 scale RC frame designed for gravity loads only and tested by Calvi et al. (2003). Reinforced concrete frames typical of Italy (1950s–1970s), designed for gravity loads only. Masonry infill provides additional stiffness and strength. Uses smooth bars with insufficient detailing and anchorage.
Description of Model: 3D finite element model of a 3-story, 3-bay moment-resisting frame with fiber-section forceBeamColumn elements, zero-length joint rotational springs (Pinching4), and lumped plasticity hinges. Quasi-static cyclic pushover using opst.anlys.SmartAnalyze with displacement-controlled loading. ODB-based response collection via opst.post.CreateODB.
Suggested Model citation: O'Reilly, G. J., Sullivan, T. J. (2019). Modeling Techniques for the Seismic Assessment of Existing Italian RC Frame Structures, Journal of Earthquake Engineering, 23(8), pp.1262–1296. DOI: 10.1080/13632469.2017.1360224.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Calvi, G. M., Magenes, G., Pampanin, S. (2002). Experimental Test on a Three Storey RC Frame Designed for Gravity Only, 12th European Conference on Earthquake Engineering, London.
Notes: Port of the Tcl model by Gerard J. O'Reilly (github.com/gerardjoreilly/Numerical-Modelling-of-GLD-RC-Frames). Non-ductile detailing typical of Italian pre-1970s construction with smooth bars and end-hooks.

purpose: 2D soil-structure interaction analysis of a cut-and-cover underground box-with_leg-frame structure with diaphragm walls and base/top slabs on Winkler spring supports.
Description of Building Structural Syste: Underground Box-with_leg-frame cut-and-cover structure with reinforced concrete diaphragm walls, a top slab, and a base slab, supported on compression-only Winkler springs representing surrounding soil.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model using dispBeamColumn elements for diaphragm walls (32 elements each), top slab (9 elements), and base slab (9 elements), with ENT (Elastic No Tension) uniaxial materials for horizontal and vertical Winkler springs across 5 soil layers. Two load cases: uniform earth pressure (15 kPa) and hydrostatic water pressure (triangular distribution). Static analysis with gravity freeze then lateral load application using opst.anlys.SmartAnalyze.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: NA
Notes: ST31 (L1) underground box-with_leg-frame model with two selectable lateral load cases: case 1 = uniform earth pressure (15 kPa), case 2 = hydrostatic water pressure (triangular). Model uses --case argument to switch.

purpose: Nonlinear dynamic earthquake and pushover analysis of a 4-story 3-bay steel special moment frame (SMF) with panel zones and IMK springs to study seismic collapse capacity.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 4-story, 3-bay steel special moment-resisting frame (SMF) per AISC 341 seismic provisions with W14 columns (W14x68 upper stories, W14x132 lower stories) and W21 beams with Reduced Beam Section (RBS) connections. An elastic gravity frame (EGF) leaning column captures P-Delta effects from tributary gravity loads. Column splices located at mid-height of stories 3-4.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model with 16 panel zones (ConstructPanel_Rectangle parallelogram model), Skiadopoulos-Elkady-Lignos Hysteretic panel zone springs (Spring_PZ), and IMKBilin rotational springs (Spring_IMK) at all beam and column ends calibrated with Lignos-Krawinkler (2011) and Lignos et al. (2019) regression equations. Column elastics use ModElasticBeam2d with stiffness modifier n=10. Gravity uses SmartAnalyze (load-controlled static); dynamic uses DynamicAnalysisCollapseSolverX with Newmark integration, Rayleigh damping zeta=2% applied to modes 1 and 3. ODB response collection via opst.post.CreateODB.
Lateral system: Special Moment-Resisting Frame (SMF) with RBS connections and panel zones
Suggested Model citation: Elkady, A. and Lignos, D.G. (2014). Modeling of the Composite Action in Fully Restrained Beam-to-Column Connections: Implications in the Seismic Design and Collapse Capacity of Steel Special Moment Frames. Earthquake Engineering & Structural Dynamics 43(13).
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Lignos, D.G. and Krawinkler, H. (2011). Deterioration Modeling of Steel Components in Support of Collapse Prediction of Steel Moment Frames under Earthquake Loading. Journal of Structural Engineering 137(11). Lignos, D.G. et al. (2019). Proposed Updates to the ASCE 41 Nonlinear Modeling Parameters for Wide-Flange Steel Columns. Journal of Structural Engineering 145(9). Skiadopoulos, A., Elkady, A. and Lignos, D.G. (2020). Proposed Panel Zone Model for Seismic Design of Steel MRFs. ASCE Journal of Structural Engineering.
Notes: Converted from original Tcl script (SMF4B.tcl) by Dr. Ahmed Elkady. All units converted from imperial (ksi, inches, kips) to N-mm-MPa. Model folder contains all Python helper modules (spring_imk, spring_pz, constructpanel_rectangle, etc.) and ground motion file NR94cnp.txt.

purpose: Nonlinear dynamic time-history analysis of a 6-story 5-bay steel concentrically-braced frame with rocking, PT strands, and fuse assemblies for seismic collapse assessment.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 6-story, 5-bay by 5-bay steel concentrically-braced frame with rocking connections consisting of pinned column bases, PT (post-tensioning) strands, and replaceable fuse assemblies. The rocking mechanism allows controlled uplift under seismic loading, with self-centering capability provided by PT strands and energy dissipation through steel fuse elements.
Description of Model: 3D finite element model using elasticBeamColumn elements for beams, columns, and braces with 12 section definitions. Rocking connections modeled with ENT base springs and twoNodeLink elements. PT strands as truss elements with ElasticPP material. Fuse assemblies use SelfCentering (gap) and Steel01 uniaxial materials in zeroLength elements. Rayleigh damping applied to modes 1 and 3. Gravity: manual LoadControl loop with Linear algorithm (SmartAnalyze Static incompatible — forces DisplacementControl). Dynamic: SmartAnalyze Transient with Newmark integration and UniformExcitation ground motion input. ODB response collection via opst.post.CreateODB with selective element tags and throttled fetch (every 10th step) for performance.
Lateral system: Concentrically-Braced Frame (CBF) with rocking, PT strands, and fuses
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Homorzabad, S. (2021). CRSBF-NDAP.py — optimization framework for concentrically-braced frames with rocking.
Notes: Converted from original CRSBF-NDAP.py script by S. Homorzabad. All units converted to N-mm-MPa. Ground motion file stored in ground_motions/ subfolder. LESSONS LEARNED: (1) SmartAnalyze Static forces DisplacementControl — LoadControl gravity must use manual ops.analyze() loop (exception documented in AGENT.md v1.6.0 §3c/§10). (2) ODB fetch_response_step() throttled to every 10th step with selective element tags to avoid hang on 2500-step transient analysis (guidance in AGENT.md §3d).

purpose: Nonlinear gravity + eigen analysis of a 5-storey infilled RC frame (Archetype 1, GLD) with masonry infill struts for seismic assessment of existing Italian construction.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 5-storey, 8x4-bay 3D RC moment-resisting frame designed for gravity loads only (GLD), typical of Italian pre-1970s construction. Masonry infill walls provide additional stiffness via equivalent diagonal struts. Smooth bars with end-hooks, non-ductile detailing. Columns: 300x300mm (stories 1-2) and 200x200mm (stories 3-5). Beams: 500x300mm throughout.
Description of Model: 3D finite element model with lumped-plasticity forceBeamColumn elements (Pinching4 hinges), zero-length joint rotational springs (Hysteretic material), and masonry infill struts (single diagonal, Pinching4 material). Grid: 8 columns x 4 rows, bay widths 3.5-20.0m X, 3.0-9.0m Y. Four infill failure modes: compression centre, compression corner, shear sliding, diagonal tension. Drift limits from Sassun et al. (2015). Gravity: manual LoadControl loop (SmartAnalyze Static incompatible). Eigen: ops.eigen(). Response collection via opst.post.CreateODB (Zarr/ODB-based for opstool >= 1.0).
Lateral Loading: Gravity + eigen only (dynamic hook for future Master script)
Suggested Model citation: Nafeh, A. M. B. (2020). Infilled-RC-Building-Database. IUSS Pavia. Hak et al. (2012). Sassun et al. (2015).
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Nafeh, A. M. B. (2020). Seismic Assessment of Infilled RC Frame Buildings. PhD Thesis, IUSS Pavia. O'Reilly, G. J., Sullivan, T. J. (2019) J. Earthquake Eng., 23(8), 1262-1296.
Notes: Port of arch_1_5st.tcl from Infilled-RC-Building-Database. All Tcl reference files preserved in tcl_reference/. Units: N-mm-MPa-tonne. Uses opstool >= 1.0 post.CreateODB API (Zarr/ODB backend). Helper modules (joint_model.py, rc_bc_non_duct.py, infill.py) are model-local ports from Tcl procedures. Gravity per AGENT.md §3c exception (manual LoadControl loop). Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py.

purpose: Static pushover analysis of a single-bay single-story 3D steel moment-resisting frame with Modified Ibarra-Krawinkler (Bilin) concentrated plastic hinges for collapse assessment.
Description of Building Structural Syste: Single-bay, single-story steel moment-resisting frame with W10X33 beams and box-section columns (b=8.02 in, t=0.35 in). The frame is a simplified test case from the WoodFrameBuildingTool suite developed by Xiaolei Xiong (Tongji University) based on the original modelling framework by Henry Burton (Stanford University).
Description of Model: 3D finite element model (ndm=3, ndf=6) using elasticBeamColumn elements for beams and columns with zero-length concentrated rotational springs at all member ends. Plastic hinges use the Bilin uniaxial material (Modified Ibarra-Krawinkler deterioration model) with parameters calibrated from Lignos & Krawinkler (2011) empirical regression equations for steel W-sections. Rigid diaphragm constraint at roof level via equalDOF. Gravity: manual LoadControl loop (SmartAnalyze Static incompatible — see AGENT.md §3c exception). Pushover: SmartAnalyze Static with DisplacementControl to 10% drift. Response collection via opst.post.CreateODB (Zarr/ODB backend). Original Tcl reference files preserved in ref/ subdirectory.
Suggested Model citation: Xiong, X., and Burton, H. (2017). WoodFrameBuildingTool — A parametric OpenSees modelling framework for wood and steel moment-resisting frames. Tongji University / Stanford University.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Ibarra, L. F., and Krawinkler, H. (2005). Global collapse of frame structures under seismic excitations. Technical Report 152, Stanford. Lignos, D. G., and Krawinkler, H. (2011). Deterioration Modeling of Steel Components in Support of Collapse Prediction of Steel Moment Frames under Earthquake Loading. ASCE Journal of Structural Engineering, 137(11), pp. 1291-1302.
Notes: Converted from original Tcl scripts in Xiaolei MomentFrame/ directory. Single-bay single-story simplified test case (NStory=0, NBase=1, XBay=1, ZBay=1). Original unit system: kips, inches, seconds — all values converted to N, mm, MPa. Reference Tcl files, Database.csv, and supporting files preserved in ref/ directory. Gravity uses manual LoadControl loop per AGENT.md §3c exception. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py.

purpose: Eigenvalue analysis and static pushover of a 2D single-story single-bay steel special moment frame with leaning column for P-Delta effects. Part of the Guan et al. (2020) database of 621 steel SMF buildings.
Description of Building Structural Syste: Single-story, single-bay steel special moment-resisting frame (SMF) with W14x370 columns and W36x160 beam. A leaning column with gravity loads captures P-Delta effects. Designed in accordance with modern codes and standards (ASCE 7).
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) using elasticBeamColumn elements for frame members and leaning column. Zero-length spring at leaning column top (stiff UX/UY, soft RZ) creates pin connection. Rigid truss transfers lateral displacements from frame to leaning column. Floor diaphragm via equalDOF. Four load patterns: dead (101), live (102), earthquake lateral (103), and combined gravity+EQ (104). Gravity: manual LoadControl loop with Newton algorithm. Pushover: SmartAnalyze Static with DisplacementControl to 5% drift. Eigenvalue analysis for modal periods. Response collection via opst.post.CreateODB (Zarr/ODB backend).
model generator: Guan et al. (2020) database generation framework
Suggested Model citation: Guan, X., Burton, H., Shokrabadi, M. (2020). A Database of Seismic Designs, Nonlinear Models, and Seismic Responses for Steel Moment Resisting Frame Buildings. DesignSafe-CI, DOI: 10.17603/ds2-8yc7-1285.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Guan, X., Burton, H., Shokrabadi, M. (2020). DOI: 10.17603/ds2-8yc7-1285. DesignSafe-CI Project PRJ-2048.
Notes: Converted from original Tcl snippet files (Building 10, DynamicAnalysis). Original unit system: kips, inches, seconds — all values converted to N, mm, MPa. Reference Tcl files preserved in ref/ directory. Missing shared library procedures (SectionProperty, rotLeaningCol) reconstructed from AISC section database and standard OpenSees practice. Section properties for W14x370, W14x455, W36x160 from AISC nominal values. Gravity uses manual LoadControl loop per AGENT.md §3c exception. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py.

purpose: Pushover, dynamic time-history, and eigenvalue analysis of a 9-story 3-bay 2D steel SMF with plastic hinges, rigid panel zone joints, and leaning column. Building 1002 from the Guan et al. (2020) database.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 9-story, 3-bay steel special moment-resisting frame with W14 columns (W14x145–W14x730) and W21–W36 beams (W21x93–W36x262). Column splices at multiple levels with varying section sizes. A leaning column at each floor carries gravity loads and captures P-Delta effects.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with 210 nodes using elasticBeamColumn elements for all frame members and leaning column. Rigid joints via equalDOF master-slave constraints replace the original 8-element panel zone rectangles. Steel01 bilinear hinges at all beam and column ends calibrated from IMK Lignos-Krawinkler (2011) regression equations with n=10 stiffness modification. Three variants: model_pushover.py (SmartAnalyze Static, 156 steps to 156 in target), model_dynamic.py (SmartAnalyze Transient with Newmark, 2000-step ground motion, Rayleigh damping 2%), model_eigen.py (gravity + eigenvalue with ODB-based eigen visualisation).
Earthquake records: Synthetic Ricker wavelet (model_dynamic.py); real records may be substituted via ground_motions/
model generator: Guan et al. (2020) database generation framework
Suggested Model citation: Guan, X., Burton, H., Shokrabadi, M. (2020). A Database of Seismic Designs, Nonlinear Models, and Seismic Responses for Steel Moment Resisting Frame Buildings. DesignSafe-CI, DOI: 10.17603/ds2-8yc7-1285.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Guan, X., Burton, H., Shokrabadi, M. (2020). DOI: 10.17603/ds2-8yc7-1285. Lignos, D.G. and Krawinkler, H. (2011). Deterioration Modeling of Steel Components, ASCE Journal of Structural Engineering 137(11).
Notes: Converted from original Tcl files (Building 1002, all three analysis types). IMKBilin replaced with Steel01 due to 2D zeroLength element compatibility issue (IMKBilin causes singular matrix in 2D). Panel zone simplified to equalDOF rigid joints for numerical robustness (original 8-element PZ had floating duplicate nodes). Eigenvalue analysis produces spurious stiff constraint modes when run after gravity — run before gravity with Plain constraints for accurate structural periods. Reference Tcl files and Database.csv in ref/ organized by analysis type. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model_pushover.py (or model_dynamic.py / model_eigen.py).

purpose: Cyclic tension force-deformation analysis of 19 bolted-bolted steel angles using a zeroLengthSection fiber model with experimentally calibrated SteelMPF materials per Beland et al. (2019).
Description of Building Structural Syste: Single bolted-bolted steel angle connection component. The vertical leg is assumed connected to a rigid member (e.g. a stiff column), and tension is applied to the outstanding leg. 19 angle sizes tested: L4x4x5/16 through L8x6x3/4.
Description of Model: 2D zeroLengthSection model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with two coincident nodes (fixed + loaded). A single fiber at the origin captures the axial force-deformation behavior using a Parallel composite of soft Elastic (numerical stability), ENT (bolt bearing), and a MinMax->Fatigue->SteelMPF chain. Each test case has its own calibrated SteelMPF parameters from Beland et al. (2019). Cyclic loading follows FEMA 350 protocol (half cycles) with displacement-controlled SmartAnalyze. ODB-based response collection via opst.post.CreateODB. Original imperial units (ksi, in, kip) converted to N, mm, MPa.
Suggested Model citation: Beland, T., Bradley, C., Tremblay, R., Rogers, C.A. (2019). Experimental calibration of bolted angle connection behavior for seismic applications.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: NA
Notes: Converted from original Tcl model (A-MainScript.tcl + Procedures/). 19 test cases run sequentially; use --tc N to run a single case. Reference Tcl files preserved in ref/ directory. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py

purpose: Nonlinear dynamic time-history analysis of an 8-story RC core wall building under the WELL1p0_1_10_1 ground motion to study seismic performance of reinforced concrete walls with confined boundary elements.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 8-story reinforced concrete core wall building. Wall is 7000 mm wide x 500 mm thick with confined boundary zones (1050 mm wide x 347.6 mm deep) at each end. Story heights: 4000 mm (ground), 3600 mm (typical). Total building height: 29,200 mm. Building width: 10,160 mm (400 in). P-Delta leaning column on the right side represents gravity framing.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model with 160 dispBeamColumn fiber-section elements (5 Lobatto IPs each, Lobatto integration), 160 zeroLength rotational springs, 8 elasticBeamColumn P-Delta leaning column elements, and 8 rigid truss diaphragm elements. Wall cross-section discretized at 200 mm vertically with 19 wall edge nodes per story. 160 material groups (15 materials each): Concrete02 (confined/unconfined), Steel02 with MinMax wrappers, Parallel composites, and elastic shear springs. Rayleigh damping 2% on modes 1 and 3. Ground motion via UniformExcitation with Path time series. Gravity: manual LoadControl loop (AGENT.md §3c exception). Dynamic: SmartAnalyze Transient with Newmark integration, 8000 steps at dt=0.005s. ODB response collection throttled every 10th step for performance.
Suggested Model citation: Shegay et al. (2019) -- RC core wall seismic performance.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: Shegay, A. et al. (2019). Seismic performance of RC core wall buildings. University of Auckland.
Notes: Converted from 37K-line Tcl model (NZ.tcl) with 800 material groups, 800 fiber sections, and 322 elements fully unrolled. Python conversion uses loop-based generation (~650 lines) with formula-derived tags matching Tcl's 3-range scheme. Key lessons: (1) Tcl massed only left master nodes — massing both sides doubles translational mass; (2) PDelta column E and I values were swapped in initial conversion; (3) OpenSeesPy beamIntegration('Lobatto') shares one section across all IPs (vs Tcl's per-IP sections), causing ~11% T1 stiffness difference; (4) ODB throttling (ODB_EVERY_N=10) essential for 8000-step transient — reduces I/O from hours to minutes; (5) node_tags filtering in CreateODB breaks opstool mesh rendering — use full tracking for visualization models. Standalone post_process.py reads existing ODB for re-visualization without re-running solver. Ground motion in ground_motions/ subfolder. Run with: uv run python models/shegay2019/model.py

purpose: Nonlinear dynamic time-history analysis of a 12-story MDOF shear-building model with bilinear hysteretic story springs for seismic uncertainty quantification via SimCenter EE-UQ.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 12-story MDOF stick/shear-building model representing a multi-story structure with concentrated story stiffness, strength, and mass. Each story exhibits bilinear hysteretic behavior (Steel01) in both horizontal directions with 2% Rayleigh damping on modes 1 and 3.
Description of Model: 2D finite-element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with 13 nodes (base + 12 floors) connected by twoNodeLink elements. Each link contains Steel01 bilinear springs for X and Y shear, plus rigid elastic springs for vertical and rotational DOFs. Lumped mass at each floor. Ground motion via UniformExcitation. Dynamic analysis with SmartAnalyze Transient + Newmark integration. ODB-based response collection via opst.post.CreateODB. EDPs: PID (peak inter-story drift) and PFA (peak floor acceleration) for all 12 stories in both directions.
Earthquake records: PEER NGA-West2 (RSN6–RSN97); synthetic Ricker wavelet for testing
Suggested Model citation: Zhong, K. (2022). MDOF building model for seismic UQ. Stanford University / SimCenter.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: NA
Notes: Converted from SimCenter EE-UQ MDOF_BuildingModel Tcl reference files (tcl_ref/newmark_solver.tcl, MyRecorder.tcl, MyPostprocess.tcl). Original units: kips, inches, seconds — all values converted to N, mm, MPa. Module-level constants in Parameters section expose all random variables (w, kx, ky, Fyx, Fyy, HRx, HRy). Reference Tcl files preserved in tcl_ref/ subdirectory. Ground motion .AT2 files from PEER must be placed in ground_motions/. Synthetic Ricker wavelet used by default for testing. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py

purpose: Nonlinear dynamic time-history analysis of a 3-story, 4-bay steel moment-resisting frame (pre-Northridge SAC/FEMA Phase II) with fiber-section beam-column elements for seismic collapse assessment.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 3-story, 4-bay steel moment-resisting frame designed per pre-Northridge Los Angeles SAC/FEMA Phase II specifications. W14 columns (W14x257 exterior, W14x311 interior) and W24–W33 beams (W33x118 floor-2, W30x116 floor-3, W24x68 roof). Beam yield strength 36 ksi, column yield strength 54 ksi. Rigid floor diaphragms via equalDOF constraints. PDelta effects included on all elements.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with 16 nodes and 21 nonlinearBeamColumn elements (12 columns + 9 beams). Fiber-discretised W-sections using patch quad (28 fibers per section: 6 web-depth, 2 web-thickness, 4 flange-width, 2 flange-thickness). Steel02 material for both beams (Fy=36 ksi) and columns (Fy=54 ksi) with 0.3% strain hardening. PDelta geometric transformation throughout. Rayleigh damping 5% on modes 1 and 3. UniformExcitation in X-direction. SmartAnalyze Transient with Newmark integration and multi-algorithm fallback (KrylovNewton, Newton, Newton-initial, ModifiedNewton, NewtonLineSearch). Collapse detection at 80% inter-story drift ratio. ODB response collection via opst.post.CreateODB. EDPs: PID, PFA, PFB, PRD, collapse status (SimCenter EE-UQ compatible).
Earthquake records: FEMA/SAC LA 10-in-50 (44 record pairs, dt=0.0025-0.02s, 1800-18000 pts); synthetic Ricker wavelet for testing
Suggested Model citation: Khajehhesameddin, P. (2014). 3-Story 4-Bay Steel Moment-Resisting Frame Model for Seismic Collapse Assessment. NEES Project Model-93, Purdue University.
Links to Papers / Design Reports: FEMA-355-C (2000). State of the Art Report on Systems Performance of Steel Moment Frames Subject to Earthquake Ground Shaking. SAC Joint Venture. FEMA-440 (2005). Improvement of Nonlinear Static Seismic Analysis Procedures, Appendix F.
Notes: Converted from NEES Model-93 Tcl reference files (ModelComponent-6/Model.tcl, Analysis_Dynamic.tcl, Wsection_S.tcl). All imperial units (kips, inches, ksi) converted to N, mm, MPa. Original Tcl files preserved in Model-93_Tcl/. Ground motion records from FEMA/SAC Phase II (44 LA pairs). Ground motion MUST be defined after gravity because ops.loadConst() freezes UniformExcitation to t=0 — see AGENT.md §12i. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py

purpose: Textbook-example dynamic time-history analysis of a 2D elastic three-bar truss under static preload followed by El Centro (NS, factor 3.0) ground motion.
Description of Building Structural Syste: 2D three-bar elastic truss with pinned base supports. Left diagonal (A=10 in²), middle vertical (A=5 in²), and right diagonal (A=5 in²) truss elements connect to a common apex node. Elastic material with E=3000 ksi.
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=2) with 4 nodes and 3 Truss elements. Single elastic material. Static point load (100 kip X, -50 kip Y) at apex frozen with loadConst. El Centro NS ground motion (factor 3.0, dt=0.01s, 20 s) via UniformExcitation in X. Dynamic analysis with SmartAnalyze Transient + Newmark integration. ODB response collection via opst.post.CreateODB. EDPs: peak apex displacements and base reactions.
Earthquake records: El Centro 1940 NS component (dt=0.01s, 3219 pts, factor 3.0, first 2000 pts used)
Links to Papers / Design Reports: XMU Finite Element Analysis course, Chapter 2.
Notes: Converted from tcl_ref/model.tcl (XMU Chapter 2 textbook example). All imperial units (kips, inches, ksi) converted to N, mm, MPa. ndf=2 model (no rotational DOFs). Ground motion file (elcentro.txt) in ground_motions/. Ground motion defined AFTER gravity per AGENT.md §12i. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py

purpose: Textbook-example dynamic time-history analysis of a 2D elastic cantilever column (2-DOF system) under Tabas earthquake with Rayleigh damping (2% on mode 1).
Description of Building Structural Syste: 2D cantilever column (0.5m × 0.5m square section, A=0.25 m², I=5.2e-3 m⁴, 6m total height) with lumped masses at mid-height and top (10,000 kg each). Elastic material with E=30 GPa (concrete).
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with 3 nodes and 2 elasticBeamColumn elements. Fixed base with lumped masses at nodes 2 (mid) and 3 (top). Static vertical preload (100 kN each floor) frozen with loadConst. Tabas earthquake (dt=0.02s, 20s) via UniformExcitation in X. Rayleigh damping 2% on mode 1 (stiffness-proportional only, a0=0). SmartAnalyze Transient with Newmark integration. ODB via opst.post.CreateODB. EDPs: inter-story drifts, peak roof displacement, peak base shear.
Earthquake records: Tabas 1978 Iran (dt=0.02s, 2501 pts, first 1000 pts used, factor=g)
Links to Papers / Design Reports: XMU Finite Element Analysis course, Chapter 4.1.
Notes: Converted from model.tcl (XMU Chapter 4.1 example). Original units: N, m, kg, Pa (SI) — converted to N, mm, MPa. Key lesson: units.py Pa = N/mm² = 1.0 (actually 1 MPa, NOT 1 Pascal). SI Pa→N-mm requires ÷1e6, but using units.py Pa gives wrong result. Use MPa directly for stress, m2/m4 helpers for area/inertia, and ÷1000 for mass (kg→tonne). Ground motion defined AFTER gravity per AGENT.md §12i. Run with: conda activate opensy && python model.py

purpose: Textbook-example dynamic time-history analysis of a single-story single-bay portal frame with Steel01 bilinear columns and elastic beam under Tabas earthquake (Rayleigh damping 2% on mode 1).
Description of Building Structural Syste: Single-story single-bay portal frame (12.80m wide x 10.97m tall). Columns use an Aggregator section: Steel01 (Fy=14.7 MPa, E=5.74 GPa, b=0.01) for flexure and Elastic (E=46.2 GPa) for axial response. Beam uses an elastic section (E=24.9 GPa, A=3.72 m², I=1.8413 m⁴).
Description of Model: 2D finite element model (ndm=2, ndf=3) with 4 nodes and 3 nonlinearBeamColumn elements (5 integration points each). Fixed column bases with lumped masses at top nodes (80 tonnes each, X-direction only). Uniform downward load on beam (-122.5 N/mm) applied via static analysis then frozen with loadConst. Tabas earthquake (dt=0.02s, 20s) via UniformExcitation in X. Rayleigh damping 2% on mode 1 (stiffness-proportional only). Dynamic analysis with SmartAnalyze Transient + Newmark integration. ODB response collection via opst.post.CreateODB.
Earthquake records: Tabas 1978 Iran (dt=0.02s, 2501 pts, first 1000 pts used, factor=g)
